newsitem.title: USA: CNF Emery unit nets $1.7 bln contract.
newsitem.headline: CNF Emery unit nets $1.7 bln contract.

text.p: CNF Transportation Inc said Wednesday its Emery Worldwide Airlines business has received a $1.7 billion contract for the sorting and transportation of priority mail from the U.S. Postal Service.
The 58 month contract is the largest in CNF's history and will involve all of its principal air, trucking and logistics operating companies.
Under terms of the deal, Emery Worldwide Airlines will obtain, equip and fully staff 10 priority mail processing plants in major metropolitan areas along the eastern seaboard.

The company will begin to create the network in July. Under the contract, the sortation and transportation network must be operational within 10 months after July and continue for four years. It has two three-year renewal options.
The total network, to be operated by CNF's Menlo Logistics, will employ more than 1,400 full-time employees and up to 1,000 more during the high-volume Christmas season.
Emery Worldwide Airlines will provide a dedicated fleet of at least 18 aircraft to transport Priority Mail and commercial air carriers will supplement Emery's fleet as necessary.

A fleet of more than 400 trucks with the USPS logo will be used to transport Priority Mail from post offices to the regional sortation centers. Con-Way Truckload will be used for linehaul transportation along the eastern seaboard.

"We are extremely pleased to continue a relationship with the U.S. Postal Service that dates back to the 1930s when we helped transport the mail to and from Alaska," said Chief Executive Donald Moffitt.
Allen Kane, chief marketing officer for the Postal Service, said priority mail is a fast growing business which generated $3.4 billion in revenues last year.
